info.title: eBPFsentinel Agent API
info.description:
REST API for the eBPFsentinel network security agent.

Provides endpoints for managing firewall rules, IPS/IDS policies, rate limiting, L7 filtering, threat intelligence, alerts, and audit logs.

Most endpoints require authentication via JWT Bearer token or API key.

get.summary:
Returns the agent's identity metadata, including the operator-managed
flag and the optional operator UI deep-link URL.
get.description:
Hot-reloadable: a config reload that toggles `management.operator_managed`
or updates `management.operator_endpoint` is reflected on the next
request without restart.

get.summary: Returns the current agent status including version, uptime, and eBPF state.
`GET /api/v1/alerts` - query stored alerts with optional filters.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of time range (nanoseconds since epoch, inclusive).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of time range (nanoseconds since epoch, inclusive).

parameters.name: technique
parameters.description: Filter by MITRE ATT&CK technique ID (e.g. "T1041").

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Filter by triage status ("open", "acknowledged", "investigating",
"resolved"). An alert nobody touched is open.

get.description:
Server-side filtering happens on every alert before it is forwarded.
Reconnects can pass `Last-Event-ID` to backfill missed alerts from
the in-memory replay buffer (≤ 5 000 events). Lagged subscribers
silently skip the gap; clients should refetch via
`GET /api/v1/alerts` to backfill in that case.

200.description: SSE stream of `event: alert` frames; `:keepalive` every 15 s

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/alerts/triage` - apply one change to many alerts.

200.description: Which alerts changed and which the store no longer holds

400.description: No IDs, too many IDs, or an invalid change

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/alerts/{id}/false-positive` - mark an alert as false positive.

patch.summary:
`PATCH /api/v1/alerts/{id}/triage` - change one alert's status or
assignee, or append a note to it.

200.description: The alert's triage after the change

400.description: Unknown status, empty change, or a value past its ceiling

put.summary: `PUT /api/v1/aliases/{id}/content` - push content for an External alias.

400.description: Invalid content or alias is not External

parameters.name: section
parameters.description: Configuration key, dotted for a nested one

403.description: Configuration writes are not enabled on this agent

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/conntrack/events` - Server-Sent Events stream of
conntrack lifecycle events (new / update / destroy).
get.description:
The poller diffs conntrack snapshots every 2 s and
pushes changes into a broadcast channel. Each SSE client receives
a copy. Lagged clients silently skip missed events.

200.description: SSE stream of `event: new`, `event: update` and `event: destroy` frames. Each frame's `data` is one JSON object carrying `event_type` and the `connection` it happened to; `:keepalive` is sent every 15 s.

404.description: Conntrack event stream not enabled, which is what a host answers when the poller has no table to read: neither `/proc/net/nf_conntrack` nor a `conntrack -L` this agent is allowed to run. A kernel built without `CONFIG_NF_CONNTRACK_PROCFS` still streams where conntrack-tools answer, so the missing proc file is not on its own the reason

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: Reverse lookup: find domains for this IP.

200.description: Kernel helper support as probed at startup

`GET /api/v1/firewall/workload/reach` - what the workload policy lets a

parameters.name: pid
parameters.description:
Answer for the task carrying this pid, reading its facts out of the
process table. Every other parameter is ignored when it is given.

parameters.name: container_name
parameters.description: Container name, as the runtime enricher reads it.

200.description: Rules naming the workload, in kernel order

404.description: No such task in the process table

503.description: The workload firewall is not loaded

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/firewall/workload/rules` - the workload rules in force and
what each has refused.

200.description: The workload rules in force, in kernel order

503.description: The workload firewall is not loaded

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: IP address to resolve (IPv4 or IPv6).

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/ips/blacklist` - manually add an IP to the IPS blacklist.
post.description:
Drives the same `add_to_blacklist` path the DNS-blocklist and reputation
auto-block features already use, so the entry is visible via `GET` and
subject to the policy's TTL cap + expiry sweeper.

400.description: Invalid IP address or blacklist full

delete.summary: `DELETE /api/v1/ips/blacklist/{ip}` - remove an IP from the IPS blacklist.

get.summary: `GET /api/v1/ips/domain-blocks` - list IPS blacklist entries originating from domain mechanisms.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/lb/vips` - apply a new VIP announce configuration.

`POST /api/v1/lb/vips/grant` - grant or release the speaker role of an
`elected` node.
post.description:
The elector calls it again before the grant runs out; a node that hears
nothing falls silent on its own clock. Only a change of speaker is
audited, never a renewal, so the trail records who answered for the
address and not every heartbeat.

400.description: Node is not elected, or the grant is too long

404.description: Learning mode is turned off on this node

200.description: The window that is now open

400.description: A scope or a duration the node cannot honour

Serves Prometheus metrics in `OpenMetrics` text format.
Readiness probe - returns 200 when eBPF programs are loaded, 503 otherwise.

ip.description: IP address to blacklist (IPv4 or IPv6).

ttl_secs.description:
Optional TTL in seconds. Defaults to - and is capped at - the policy's
maximum blacklist duration.

AgentIdentityResponse.description:
Operator-managed metadata advertised to the dashboard, plus the
minimum identity fields needed to identify the agent uniquely.

Read-only view of the agent's `management` config block; both fields
are hot-reloadable via the existing config reload mechanism.

hostname.description: `gethostname()` at startup; surfaces the host running the agent.

operator_endpoint.description:
Optional URL the operator exposes (typically a Kubernetes-native
UI). The dashboard deep-links to this URL from the
"operator-managed" badge.

operator_managed.description:
`true` when the agent's configuration is owned by the Kubernetes
operator (CRD-driven). The dashboard locks its config-edit UI on
agents reporting `true` to prevent two-way drift.

version.description: Build version of the running agent (`CARGO_PKG_VERSION`).

container_coverage.description: What the agent sees of the containers on this node.

status.description:
Coarse lifecycle state: `running` once eBPF programs are attached,
`degraded` while operating without them (userspace-only fallback).

AlertNoteResponse.description: One note on an alert as the API writes it.

author.description: Who the caller said wrote it.

via.description: The identity the agent authenticated the write under.

oneOf.description: Container identity resolved from the event's `cgroup_id` (if any).

data_type.description: DLP: data category (pci, pii, credentials, custom).

executable_dev.description: DLP: device number of that binary, present with `executable_path`.

executable_inode.description:
DLP: inode of that binary, present with `executable_path`. The pair
identifies the file even where the path was reused.

executable_path.description:
DLP: the binary the writing process was running, read from
`/proc/<pid>/exe` at alert time. Absent when the process was already
gone, which is the honest answer rather than a guessed name.

executable_source.description: DLP: how the executable was obtained - `process_at_alert_time`.

flow_source.description:
DLP: how the five-tuple was obtained - `kernel_socket` when the probe
read it off the socket, `task_socket_correlation` when it came from
the same task's last socket. Absent means the addresses and ports are
zero because nothing was resolved, not because the peer is 0.0.0.0.

notes.description: What people wrote on it, oldest first.

src_addr.description:
Source address as four big-endian u32 words.
IPv4: `[v4, 0, 0, 0]`. IPv6: full 128-bit address.

status.description: Where the alert stands in the queue; `open` until somebody moves it.

triage_updated_ns.description: When the triage last changed (nanoseconds since epoch).

oneOf.description:
The process behind the flow, where the node could name one. Absent
for a flow it only forwarded, for a socket opened before the hooks
attached, and on a host whose kernel refused them.

AttachBlockEntry.description: One attach the kernel refused, and what is standing in the way.

nested_xdp.description:
True when the interface already carries somebody else's XDP program,
the nested-XDP case that Docker and Kubernetes produce.

reason.description:
Operator-readable sentence: what the kernel said, translated against
what is actually on the interface right now.

AttributionReport.description: What became of the cgroup socket hooks on this host.

attached.description:
True only when every hook attached. A partial set is reported as not
attached, because half the hooks make an absent workload mean two
different things with nothing on the wire to tell them apart.

brokered.description: Whether the warden created the links, which is the rootless posture.

cgroup.description: The cgroup the hooks were attached to, or asked for.

hooks.description: The hooks that attached, named as the kernel programs are.

reason.description: Why nothing is attached, in the words the attach failed with.

src_addr.description:
Source address as four big-endian u32 words.
IPv4: `[v4, 0, 0, 0]`. IPv6: full 128-bit address.

BulkTriageRequest.description: `POST /api/v1/alerts/triage` body: one change applied to many alerts.

missing.description: Alerts the store no longer holds.

updated.description: Alerts the change was applied to.

ConfigSectionWrite.description: One section of the configuration, as the editor holds it.

yaml.description:
A YAML document rooted at the section's own key, exactly as the read
route renders it, so the text an operator edited is the text that
comes back.

max_connections.description:
Conntrack table capacity - the maximum number of flows the
agent tracks before eviction (the BPF connection-table size).

oneOf.description:
The local process that opened the flow, where the socket index could
name one. A flow this node only forwarded has none, and so does one
opened before the hooks attached.

ContainerCoverage.description:
What this agent can say about the containers it sees.

Every field is a verdict rather than a setting: the procfs actually being
read, whether it is the host's, and what each enricher decided.

host_proc.description:
`proc_root` is a mounted host procfs rather than this process's own,
which is what covers a neighbouring container without sharing the
node's pid namespace.

proc_root.description: The procfs every container and DLP lookup is rooted on.

resolver.description: The cgroup-id resolver is running, so an alert carries a container id.

ContainerIdentity.description:
Container provenance surfaced on an alert.

The field is absent altogether for a host-namespace process, so `kind` is
always `container` where the object exists at all. It is kept because a
reader that has to tell a container apart from a host should be told so by
a value rather than by an absence it has to interpret.

The Kubernetes and the Docker halves are filled by whichever enricher
attached metadata, and never both, since the pipeline keeps the first
enricher that answered.

container_name.description: Kubernetes container name (only when a k8s enricher attached metadata).

image.description: Image tag (only when the Docker enricher attached metadata).

kind.description: Always `container`: a host-namespace process carries no identity.

name.description: Container name (only when the Docker enricher attached metadata).

namespace.description: Kubernetes namespace (only when a k8s enricher attached metadata).

pod.description: Kubernetes pod name (only when a k8s enricher attached metadata).

runtime.description: Detected runtime (docker, containerd, crio, podman, unknown).

health_check_interval_secs.description: Health-check probe interval in seconds. When set, an ICMP probe is configured.

interface.description: Egress interface; defaults to empty (inherits the agent's primary).

weight.description: Routing weight; maps to failover priority (lower = preferred).

listen_addr.description:
Destination address the service answers on, a virtual address.
Omitted, the service answers on every address on its port.

CreateNptV6RuleRequest.description: Request DTO for creating an `NPTv6` prefix translation rule.

vlan_id.description: 802.1Q VLAN ID: omit for any VLAN, 0 for untagged only, 1-4094 exact.

burst_bytes.description: Token bucket depth in bytes. Must be above 0 on a rate-limited pipe.

delay_ms.description: Added latency in milliseconds, paced on egress via the fq qdisc.

direction.description: Which hook the pipe shapes: `ingress`, `egress` or `both`.

rate_bps.description: Bandwidth limit in bits per second; `0` leaves the pipe unlimited.

src_ip.description: Source host to limit, as a bare address or a `/32`.

rate_pps.description: Rate limit in packets per second (required for `throttle_ip`).

target.description:
Target host address (e.g. `1.2.3.4` or `2001:db8::1`). The blacklist
and the rate limiter are both keyed by a single address, so a prefix
is refused rather than silently narrowed.

action.description:
`allow`, `permit` or `accept` to permit traffic; `deny`, `drop` or
`reject` to deny it. Any other word is refused.

default_policy.description:
Policy applied when no rule and no inter-zone policy decided the
packet. `allow`, `permit` and `accept` permit; `deny`, `drop` and
`reject` deny, as does an absent value. Any other word is refused.

interfaces.description:
Network interfaces grouped into this zone. A zone with no interface
carries no traffic: the datapath matches on the ingress interface.

name.description: Zone name; used as the zone identifier.

DdosAttackResponse.description: One flood the detector is tracking, or tracked until it expired.

attack_type.description:
`syn_flood`, `udp_amplification`, `icmp_flood`, `rst_flood`,
`fin_flood`, `ack_flood` or `volumetric`: the same spelling the
configuration file uses and `POST /api/v1/ddos/policies` accepts.

last_seen_ns.description:
When the detector last counted a packet against this attack. On the
history route this is where the flood stopped, which a start alone
cannot say.

src_country.description:
Source country, `null` where `GeoIP` resolved none. A policy carrying
`country_thresholds` is judged against this, and a `block` policy
injects this country's CIDRs into the firewall, so an attack with no
country here is one no country rule acted on.

attack_type.description: Spelled the way the configuration file and the create route spell it.

country_thresholds.description:
Per-country thresholds that replace `detection_threshold_pps` for
traffic from those countries, absent where the policy carries none.
Reading it back is the only way to explain a policy that fired well
under the threshold beside it.

description.description:
What the pattern is for, as the configuration file wrote it. Empty
where none was written.

mode.description:
`alert` or `block`, this pattern's own. A pattern may block while the
service default alerts, so a listing carrying only the service mode
reads as a set of patterns that all merely report.

DlpScopeResponse.description:
What the probes are reading right now.

The effective scope rather than the configured one: it is built from the
workloads the resolvers answered for, so an operator verifies the fence
instead of trusting the document.

allowed_cgroups.description: How many cgroup ids the kernel allow-list carries.

enabled.description: Whether the probes are armed at all.

mode.description:
`all` when every task on the node is read, `workloads` when the
kernel allow-list decides.

refreshed_unix.description: When the scope was last resolved, seconds since the epoch.

selectors.description: How many selectors are in force.

unselected.description:
Workloads seen and named by no rule, counted rather than listed:
on a busy node that list is the node.

DlpScopeUnmatchedResponse.description: A rule that matched nothing, and why.

reason.description: Why it matched nothing, in a sentence an operator can act on.

selector.description: The matchers it carries, as one line.

DlpScopeWorkloadResponse.description: One workload the scope decided on, as the scope route answers it.

cgroup.description: Absolute cgroup v2 path, where one was resolved.

cgroup_id.description: Cgroup id the kernel allow-list carries.

rule.description: The rule that decided it, by name.

enabled.description: Whether DNS intelligence (cache + blocklist) is enabled.

attach_blocked.description:
Attaches that lost, if any. `programs[].loaded` says a program is in
the kernel; this says whether it reached the wire.

EnricherState.description:
Where a metadata enricher ended up, as the agent decided it at startup.

The deployment matrix claims container enrichment per mode; this is the
same claim answered by the running agent, so the two can be compared on a
node instead of taken on trust.

ips.description: IP addresses/CIDRs to load into the alias.

last_fetched.description:
Unix-epoch milliseconds of the last completed feed fetch, or `null`
if no fetch has run yet. Shared across feeds (one fetch cycle).

persistent.description: Whether the cache is backed by a persistent store that survives restarts.

FlowExportStatusResponse.description: The exporter, its table and its sinks.

enabled.description:
False when no sink is configured, in which case every counter below
is zero because nothing was ever collected, not because nothing
happened.

evicted.description: Flows written out early because the table was full.

queue_drops.description:
Records built and then dropped because the queue to the sinks was
full. A number here is a collector that cannot keep up, and it is why
a missing flow is never a silence.

restarted.description:
Flows whose counters went backwards, which is a five-tuple the kernel
handed to a new connection rather than a negative.

sampled_out.description: Flows the sampling rate left out. Zero at the default rate of one.

sampling.description:
One flow in this many is exported. The collector cannot infer it, so
it has to be configured on both sides.

FlowSinkStatusResponse.description: What one sink says about itself.

detail.description:
Why it is unhealthy, in the words the transport used. Absent while it
is healthy, and it names no address beyond the sink's own name.

healthy.description: False once a write failed and before the next one succeeds.

health_status.description: Alias of `status` for clients expecting a `health_status` field.

id.description: Gateway identifier, rendered as a string for stable API addressing.

weight.description: Alias of `priority`, exposed as a routing weight.

enabled.description: Whether `GeoIP` enrichment is enabled in the agent configuration.

ready.description: Whether an mmdb-backed lookup database is loaded and ready.

HelperSupportEntry.description: One `(program type, helper)` answer from the startup probe.

country_thresholds.description:
Per-country threshold overrides, keyed by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. A
rule stricter for one country reads as a single threshold without
them.

domain_pattern.description:
Domain the rule matches on, for rules evaluated against resolved names
rather than against a port.

interfaces.description:
The interface groups this rule is scoped to, in the words the
configuration file used, `!` prefix included. Empty is a floating
rule, which sees every interface the classifier is attached to.

oneOf.description:
Present only when another rule holds a kernel map slot this rule also
claims.

src_port.description:
Source-port match, set on rules watching the reply leg of a flow. A
rule carrying one fires on nothing else, so a listing that dropped it
read as matching every port.

interfaces.description:
The interface groups this rule is scoped to, in the words the
configuration file used, `!` prefix included. Empty is a floating
rule, which enforces on every interface the classifier is on.

oneOf.description:
Present only when another rule holds a kernel map slot this rule also
claims. A prevention rule that lost its slot is never replayed in
userspace, so it blocks nothing until the conflict is resolved.

cached_count.description: Number of cached JA4S server fingerprints.

persistent.description: Whether the cache is backed by a persistent store that survives restarts.

KernelFeaturesResponse.description:
What the kernel answered when the agent probed it at startup.

`probed = false` means the probe could not run, **not** that the kernel
lacks anything: `helpers` and `missing_required` are then empty because
nothing was measured, and `reason` says why. Treating that as a capability
report would invert its meaning.

attribution.description:
Whether the socket-attribution hooks are on this host's cgroup, and
why not where they are not. Read from what the attach actually did,
not from the probe: a kernel that supports the program type can still
refuse the attach, and a flow with no workload on it is the same
silence either way.

load_mode.description:
How the agent loads its objects, which is why a probe needing
`CAP_BPF` can be unavailable on a host where every program loads.

process_signal.description:
Whether this node can stop the process behind a flow, and with what.
Reported whether or not the capability is on, because the blast radius
of an action has to be readable before somebody arms it.

process_tracing.description:
Whether the exec and exit tracepoints behind the process table are on
this host, and why not where they are not. Read the same way as the
attribution block above: from what the attach did.

quarantine.description:
Whether this node can cut a workload off the network while leaving it
running, and whether that cut reaches the flows it already holds.
Reported whether or not the capability is on, for the same reason as
the block above.

workload_firewall.description:
Whether the hooks deciding a workload rule are on this host's cgroup.
Read the same way as the two blocks above, and asked more often than
either: a rule naming a binary is the one kind of rule whose absence
nothing on the wire makes visible.

dst_ip_alias.description: The same, on the destination address.

dst_port_alias.description: The same, on the destination port.

src_country_codes.description:
ISO-3166 country codes the rule narrows its source to. A rule scoped
to a handful of countries and served without them reads as a rule
acting on every source there is.

src_ip_alias.description:
The alias the rule was declared against, in the words the
configuration file used, so a reader can find the line that wrote it.
A rule created through this API names none.

probed.description:
Whether anything ever measured the status above. A backend of a service
with no health check, a disabled backend and a backend of a disabled
service are never probed, and each of them reads `healthy` for ever.

LbHealthCheckResponse.description:
What a service is probed with, in the words the configuration file used.

The probe carries no target of its own: every enabled backend is reached on
the address and port it serves on.

oneOf.description:
The probe behind the backend statuses below, omitted where the service
carries none and nothing is ever measured.

listen_addr.description:
Destination address the service answers on, omitted when it answers
on every address on its port.

health_checked.description:
Whether the service carries a health check at all. A backend of a
service that carries none starts healthy and is never probed, so its
status is a default rather than a measurement.

listen_addr.description:
Destination address the service answers on, omitted when it answers
on every address on its port.

interface.description: L2 interface VIPs egress on. Required unless role is disabled.

vips.description:
VIPs this node owns. Must be non-empty unless role is disabled,
and ignored when it is.

seconds.description:
How long this node speaks for its VIPs unless renewed, in seconds,
at most 300. Zero releases the role at once.

arp_replies.description:
Forged ARP replies emitted for this VIP since program load
(per-CPU summed kernel counter).

self_announced.description:
Whether this VIP is currently in the self-whitelist (true when
the node is speaker and the binding has been written).

bindings_count.description:
Number of self-owned bindings registered in the kernel
`SELF_OWNED_BINDINGS` map.

grant_remaining_ms.description:
Milliseconds left on the speaker grant of an `elected` node, absent
when it holds none. The node falls silent when this reaches zero
without a renewal.

interface.description: L2 interface VIPs egress on (empty when role is disabled).

is_speaker.description: Whether this node currently answers ARP / sends gratuitous ARP.

LearningPolicyResponse.description: The allow-list a window describes, with what it took to write it.

collapsed_rules.description:
Rules whose destination was widened to a prefix. Each one names the
addresses it came from in a comment above it.

rules.description: Rules written, the closing deny of each workload included.

session.description: The window it was rendered from, as it stood at the reading.

skipped_edges.description:
Destinations no rule could be written for, because their workload
cannot be named by a selector.

yaml.description: The document, YAML in the agent's own rule schema.

LearningSessionResponse.description:
A window, as it stands.

Everything a reader needs to decide whether the document it would
produce is worth applying: how long it has really been watching, whether
the agent was up for all of it, how many destinations it holds, how many
it had to refuse, and how long since it last found a new one.

continuous.description: False once the agent has been down for part of the window.

dropped_edges.description:
Destinations refused because the window was full. Anything but zero
means the document it produces is incomplete, and it says so.

gap_secs.description: Seconds of the window the agent was not running for.

scope_description.description: The scope in one line, as the generated document states it.

MissingHelperEntry.description: A helper an object needs that this kernel does not offer for its type.

detail.description: The same fact as one sentence, for logs and support tickets.

switched_off.description:
Techniques this agent maps but whose component is switched off.

They are what the product could raise here and this configuration
does not, kept apart from `techniques` so that nobody reading the
response can count them as coverage by accident.

total_techniques.description: Total number of covered techniques (for active components).

interfaces.description:
The interface groups this rule is scoped to, in the words the
configuration file used, `!` prefix included. Empty is a floating
rule, which translates on every interface the programs are on.

match_src.description:
What the rule is narrowed to. A rule carrying none of these translates
every packet the direction carries, so each is absent rather than an
empty value a reader would take for a restriction.

match_src_alias.description:
The alias a rule still names, which is a rule whose match criteria the
alias service has not resolved into CIDRs yet.

nat_type.description:
The translation this rule performs, spelled as the configuration file
spells it: `snat`, `dnat`, `masquerade`, `one_to_one`, `redirect` or
`port_forward`.

translation.description:
What the rule rewrites to. The fields are the type's own, so a reader
sees the address and the ports the rule was written with rather than
the type word alone.

NatTranslation.description:
The addresses and ports a translation rewrites to.

Tagged with the same word `nat_type` carries, since a reader deciding what
a rule does reads the two together.

NptV6RuleResponse.description: Response DTO for an `NPTv6` prefix translation rule.

interfaces.description:
The interface groups this rule is scoped to, in the words the
configuration file used, `!` prefix included. Empty is a floating
rule, which translates on every interface the programs are on.

ProcessContainerResponse.description:
The container a process runs in, where it runs in one. Absent means the
host, which is why the field is omitted rather than filled with a name.

image.description: The image, where the enricher that answered carries one.

name.description:
The container name an enricher resolved, or the namespaced pod name
under Kubernetes. Absent when no enricher answered.

ProcessIdentityResponse.description:
What the table knows a process by. `kind` is `path` or `unknown`; the
hash of the executable is not computed yet, and when it is it arrives as
a third kind rather than as a field nobody can tell apart from absent.

path.description: The executable path, where the identity carries one.

processes.description: Newest first, so a reader watching a node sees what just started.

ProcessSignalReport.description: What this node can do to the process behind a flow.

attached.description:
True only when the capability is on in the configuration and the
tracepoint attached. False is the ordinary answer: the capability is
off unless a configuration asked for it.

protected.description:
How many thread group ids the kernel refuses to signal whatever a rule
asks, the agent's own among them.

reason.description: Why nothing can be stopped on this node, in one sentence.

signal.description: The signal a kill would send, zero when nothing is armed.

window_ms.description:
How long a target stays armed before the arming lapses. A target that
makes no syscall in that window is reported as a survivor rather than
assumed dead.

ProcessTableStatsResponse.description:
The bound and what it cost, so a reader can tell an empty table from a
full one shedding its oldest entry.

ProcessTracingReport.description: What became of the two process tracepoints on this host.

attached.description:
True only when both tracepoints attached. One of the two is reported
as not attached: a table fed by exec alone never forgets a process,
and one fed by exit alone never learns of one.

command_line.description:
Whether the table keeps command lines, which is off unless the
configuration asked for it.

reason.description: Why nothing is attached, in the words the attach failed with.

tracepoints.description: The tracepoints that attached, named as the kernel programs are.

ProcessTracingResponse.description: What the agent can say about the two tracepoints behind the table.

attached.description: Both tracepoints are attached and the table is being filled.

command_line.description:
Command lines are being kept. Off by default: an argument vector
carries secrets often enough that keeping it is a decision.

reason.description:
Why the table is empty or stale, in one sentence. `None` when
everything attached.

tracepoints.description: The tracepoints that did attach, in attach order.

interfaces.description:
The interface groups this rule is scoped to, in the words the
configuration file used, `!` prefix included. Empty is a floating
rule, which shapes every interface the programs are on.

vlan_id.description: 802.1Q VLAN ID: absent = any VLAN, 0 = untagged only, 1-4094 = exact.

direction.description: Which hook the pipe shapes: `ingress`, `egress` or `both`.

interfaces.description:
The interface groups this rule is scoped to, in the words the
configuration file used, `!` prefix included. Empty is a floating
rule, which shapes every interface the programs are on.

QuarantineReport.description: What this node can do to a workload short of stopping it.

armed.description:
True only when the capability is on in the configuration and the maps
behind it are held. False is the ordinary answer: the capability is off
unless a configuration asked for it.

protected.description:
How many cgroups are refused whatever a rule asks, the agent's own and
the hierarchy root among them.

reason.description: Why nothing can be quarantined on this node, in one sentence.

tears_down_flows.description:
Whether arming also tears down the flows the workload already holds. A
false here is the difference between a workload that can open nothing
new and one that is actually off the network.

window_ms.description:
How long a cgroup stays cut off before the arming lapses, zero when
nothing is armed. A rule may ask for less.

interfaces.description:
The interface groups this rule is scoped to, in the words the
configuration file used, `!` prefix included. Empty is a floating
rule, which meters every interface the programs are on.

attach_blocked.description:
Attachments the kernel refused, one operator-readable sentence each,
naming the program, the interface and what is holding the slot. A
non-empty list is why this host is not ready; an empty one means the
agent never lost an attach, which is a different situation from having
no programs at all.

datapath_stalled_secs.description:
How long the datapath has gone without a ring-buffer pass, in seconds,
when that is long enough to be a stall. Absent when a reader is passing
normally and absent when none has ever passed, which are two different
situations: `ebpf_loaded` and `attach_blocked` tell them apart. A value
here is a wedged reader task, and the same reading is what withholds
the service watchdog's keep-alive.

ebpf_loaded.description: Whether eBPF programs are successfully loaded.

flow_sinks_unhealthy.description:
Flow sinks that cannot currently reach their destination, by name.

Reported and deliberately not gating: a collector that stopped
answering must not take this node's traffic enforcement out of a
cluster, and a readiness probe that fails on it would do exactly
that. The name is the transport and the address the operator
configured, and the reason is on the flow export status route.

kernel_helpers_missing.description:
Helpers the startup probe found missing, one sentence each. Empty both
when the kernel offers everything and when the probe could not run -
`/api/v1/ebpf/kernel-features` distinguishes the two.

RefreshFeedRequest.description: Optional body for a feed refresh request.

feed_id.description:
Feed to refresh. Accepted for forward compatibility; the fetcher
currently refreshes every enabled feed in a single cycle.

RefreshResponse.description: Response to a feed refresh request.

RouteResponse.description: A resolved default route derived from the active gateway selection.

destination.description: Destination CIDR served by this route.

gateway_id.description: Identifier of the gateway this route egresses through.

country_codes.description:
ISO-3166 country codes this rule matches, resolved from a `GeoIP`
alias referenced by `src_alias`/`dst_alias`. Set only when the
referenced alias is a `GeoIP` kind.

interfaces.description:
The interface groups this rule is scoped to, in the words the
configuration file used, `!` prefix included. Empty is a floating
rule, which is the only thing a rule created through this API can be.

oneOf.description: Every workload on the node a flow can be attributed to.
One cgroup v2 subtree, by absolute path.
A set of workloads, named the way a rule names them.

ScopeBody.description: What the window is asked to watch.

SlotContentionResponse.description:
A kernel map slot holds one rule, so two rules watching the same port and
protocol cannot both be installed. This says which rule took the slot and
whether the loser is still evaluated.

evaluated_in_userspace.description: `false` means the rule is loaded, enabled, and matches nothing.

shadowed_by.description: Ids of the rules holding a slot this rule also claims.

interface.description:
Network interface to capture on, "any" or absent for every interface.

An absent value binds the socket to interface index 0, which is every
link on the host rather than the first one the agent is configured
for: a capture is a diagnostic and the filter is what narrows it.

snap_length.description: Snap length: max bytes per packet (default 1500).

duration_secs.description: How long to watch for, in seconds.

scope.description: What to watch. Omitted means the whole node.

TechniqueEntry.description: A single technique in the coverage matrix.

ThresholdResponse.description: Per-rule threshold/rate detection, surfaced for rate-based IDS rules.

TlsStatusResponse.description:
Per-connection TLS status, surfaced so operators can confirm the
negotiated key-exchange group (e.g. verify a post-quantum hybrid
handshake) on a live connection.

negotiated_group.description:
Negotiated TLS 1.3 key-exchange named group for this connection
(e.g. `X25519MLKEM768`, `X25519`, `secp256r1`), or `null` when the
request did not arrive over TLS.

post_quantum.description:
`true` when the negotiated group is the post-quantum hybrid
(`X25519MLKEM768`).

tls.description: Whether this request arrived over TLS.

TriageRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/alerts/{id}/triage` body. A field left out stays as it
was; `assignee: null` takes the alert off whoever held it.

author.description:
Who is writing, when a console writes on a person's behalf.
Defaults to the authenticated identity.

TriageResponse.description: The triage of one alert after a change.

UprobeEntry.description: One uprobe the DLP module currently holds a link for.

brokered.description:
`BPF_LINK_CREATE` was issued by the warden (rootless posture) rather than
by the agent itself.

dev.description: Block device of the probed file.

ino.description:
Inode of the probed file. With `dev`, the identity two runs are compared
on: the same path can name a different file after a package upgrade.

offset.description:
File offset the link was created at. A changed offset for an unchanged
inode is a resolution regression, not a new build.

path.description: Path the link was created against, as the loader saw it.

program.description: Loader name of the eBPF program behind the probe.

retprobe.description: The probe fires on return rather than on entry.

sticky.description:
The attachment survives a reconcile that finds no process mapping the
inode - the cold-start system-library fallback.

symbol.description: Exported symbol the probe sits on.

UprobeInventoryResponse.description:
The uprobe set the DLP module currently holds.

An empty list is a real answer, and always the same one: no TLS payload is
being read. It covers a DLP module that is not loaded, a scan that resolved
nothing, and a datapath that has been detached.

probes.description: Every probe, ordered by inode then symbol so two runs diff cleanly.

WorkloadFirewallReport.description: What became of the workload firewall hooks on this host.

attached.description:
True only when every hook attached. There is no optional hook here:
half the hooks is a policy that reads as in force and is not.

brokered.description: Whether the warden created the links, which is the rootless posture.

cgroup.description: The cgroup the hooks were attached to, or asked for.

hooks.description: The hooks that attached, named as the kernel programs are.

reason.description:
Why nothing is attached, in the words the attach failed with. A
document carrying no workload rule loads no object, and says so here.

WorkloadReachEntry.description: One rule naming the workload, and what it has refused.

allows.description: Whether the rule lets the destination through.

denials.description:
How many socket operations this rule has refused since it was
published, counted by the kernel.

destination.description: The destination half of the match, written out.

mode.description: `enforce` when the kernel refuses, `observe` when it only counts.

selector.description: The selector written out, as the rule names the workload.

WorkloadReachResponse.description: The answer to "what may this workload reach".

enforcing.description: Whether any rule in force has the kernel refuse rather than count.

exe.description:
The facts the rules were matched against, after the process table
filled in whatever the caller did not give.

rules.description:
Every rule naming this workload, in the order the kernel walks them.
The first one admitting the destination decides, so a rule low in
this list is a rule something above it may never reach.

WorkloadResponse.description: The process a flow belongs to, where the agent could name one.

cgroup.description: cgroup v2 id, as the kernel numbers it.

container.description: Container id, where the process runs in one.

exe.description:
The executable path the process table recorded. Forgeable by the
process itself, which is why it is a path and not an identity.

image.description: Container image, where the runtime enricher read one.

pid.description:
The process that owns the socket. Never zero: a block exists only
when there is a process to name.

pod.description: Pod name, on a Kubernetes node.

service_account.description: Service account the pod runs as, where the enricher read one.

source.description:
How the process was reached - `socket` when the kernel's own handle
on the socket answered, `flow` when the five-tuple was matched
against the index of established connections, `process` when the
event already named the task. The first and the third are read, the
second is correlated.

uid.description: The real uid of the task when the socket was opened.

unit.description: systemd unit, for a host process the agent could place in one.

WorkloadRulesResponse.description: The workload rules in force, each with what it has refused.

enforcing.description: Whether any rule in force has the kernel refuse rather than count.

rules.description: Every rule in force, in the order the kernel walks them.

WorkloadSelectorBody.description:
One of the selectors a scope is written with, in the shape a workload
rule already uses.

action.description: Alias of `policy`, exposed under the `action` field name.

api_key.name: X-API-Key
api_key.description: Static API key configured in agent

bearer_auth.description: JWT token obtained via OIDC or static configuration
